name: Lionel Woodville
summary:
Lionel Woodville was a Bishop of Salisbury in England, holding the position from 1479 until his death in 1484. He played a significant role in the Catholic Church during the late Middle Ages and was a prominent figure in the English Reformation.

Woodville's tenure as Bishop was marked by controversy, particularly with regards to his relationships with the powerful Woodville family and the influence of their descendants on the English monarchy. His most notable achievement was the establishment of the monastery at Bisham Abbey, which became a major center for learning and spirituality.

The legacy of Lionel Woodville can be seen in the impact he had on the Catholic Church and the English Reformation. He played a key role in shaping the theological debates of his time and was a vocal advocate for reform within the Church. His contributions to the establishment of Bisham Abbey helped spread learning and spirituality throughout the region.
